default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-618.title: Dollar-lead lag on the index
E-618.hypothesis: WIN and WDO trade inversely and index futures react a bit later to a dollar move; when the dollar moves more than usual and WIN has not yet followed inversely, late index participants catch up.

E-619.title: Session-open price reclaim
E-619.hypothesis: The session's opening print is a reference many traders watch; after trading on one side of it for a while, a close back across it shifts control.

E-620.title: Bollinger squeeze release
E-620.hypothesis: When closing-price dispersion is far below its usual size for the time of day, stops cluster just outside the box; a close beyond the box releases the compressed volatility.

E-621.title: Wick absorption balance
E-621.hypothesis: Persistent long lower wicks over a window show passive buyers absorbing sells; a green bar after it means the sellers are spent (mirror for upper wicks).

E-622.title: Volume-climax reversal
E-622.hypothesis: A very heavy bar that pokes to a new window extreme but closes away from it is a capitulation or exhaustion; the forced side is done, fade it.

E-623.title: EMA stretch fade in range units
E-623.hypothesis: Price stretched several average bar-ranges away from its short EMA is an overshoot from impatient market orders; fade the first bar that gets there.

E-624.title: Quiet shock bar fade
E-624.hypothesis: A bar with a much larger range than usual but below-median volume moved on thin liquidity, not on real participation; fade its direction.

E-625.title: Range-expansion triplet follow
E-625.hypothesis: Three same-colour bars with growing ranges mean participation is building in one direction; the next wave of followers keeps it going.

E-626.title: Single bar through VWAP
E-626.hypothesis: One big-body bar that opens on one side of VWAP and closes on the other is an institutional-size push through the day's fair value; follow it.

E-627.title: Previous-close line reclaim
E-627.hypothesis: The prior session settlement-like close is a reference for overnight positions; after the price stays on one side a while, a close across it shows those holders giving up or doubling down.
